requirement: Implement a fixed email-processing pipeline abstraction rather than a general-purpose workflow engine.
rationale: Keeps the first version small and aligned with known transformations

requirement: Declare the pipeline graph and step definitions in versioned Swift code and bind each step to one persisted transformerName.
rationale: Avoids a dynamic workflow-definition database and makes invalid cycles testable before release

requirement: Create one EmailProcessingStep row for every step in the selected pipeline version when creating a job.
rationale: Makes pending work and overall completion durable and inspectable

requirement: Each code-defined step lists stable prerequisite step IDs and the pipeline definition must be acyclic.
rationale: Provides explicit sequencing without persisting redundant graph definitions

requirement: A pending step becomes ready only after all declared prerequisites reach stable terminal outcomes and every required predecessor succeeded or reused a valid result; optional failed or skipped predecessors are allowed only by an explicit no-output input contract.
rationale: Prevents consumers from observing missing inputs

requirement: Run independent ready steps concurrently subject to small execution-kind concurrency limits.
rationale: Supports parallel work without an external queue

requirement: When a required prerequisite fails permanently mark dependent steps skipped with a dependency-failed reason.
rationale: Ensures the job reaches a deterministic terminal state

requirement: A step may depend on an optional predecessor only when its input contract explicitly handles that predecessor producing no output.
rationale: Avoids accidental execution with incomplete inputs

requirement: Use pending, running, blocked, succeeded, succeededWithWarnings, failed, and cancelled as job states.
rationale: Keeps overall state compact and represents missing implementations without treating them as execution failures

requirement: Use pending, ready, running, retryWaiting, blocked, succeeded, failed, skipped, cancelled, and reused as step states.
rationale: Separates schedulable retry blocked configuration and terminal outcomes

requirement: A job succeeds only when every instantiated step is terminal, every required step is succeeded or reused, and no optional step failed permanently.
rationale: Defines completion independently of optional failures

requirement: A job succeedsWithWarnings only after every instantiated step is terminal, all required steps succeeded or reused, and one or more optional steps failed permanently.
rationale: Allows best-effort transformations without hiding their failures

requirement: A required permanent failure prevents job success; skip failed dependents and cancel other unfinished work cooperatively before publishing the terminal failed job.
rationale: Provides a clear terminal rule

requirement: Commit officialStatus customStatus statusMessage outputData output metadata timestamps and the resulting step state in one background-context save.
rationale: Prevents a terminal outcome from becoming visible without its complete result

requirement: Store small transformation-specific output as versioned canonical JSON or binary Data and enable Core Data external binary storage when appropriate.
rationale: Keeps variable outputs flexible without adding a column for every transformation

requirement: Store scheduler state official status transformer name attempts versions and timestamps as normal Core Data attributes rather than JSON or Data.
rationale: Keeps lifecycle fields queryable and migration-friendly

requirement: Do not hide accountID emailUID or emailDate inside JSON or Data.
rationale: Preserves efficient filtering joining and date-range queries

requirement: Copy the persisted canonical UTC email_date into emailDate; choose it once from INTERNALDATE, then unambiguous Date, then the first metadata_fetched_at and preserve it across refreshes.
rationale: Keeps date-range queries deterministic when the Date header is missing or ambiguous

requirement: Store very large disposable artifacts in managed files and persist only an integrity-checked relative locator when Core Data external binary storage is unsuitable.
rationale: Avoids oversized database rows while keeping recovery explicit

requirement: Treat the official retry status as retryable and the official failed status as permanent; map thrown infrastructure errors through the library failure classifier.
rationale: Custom statuses never control retry behavior

requirement: Apply bounded exponential backoff with jitter and persist attemptCount maximumAttempts and nextAttemptAt.
rationale: Survives restart and avoids synchronized retry storms

requirement: Apply the same bounded retry policy to optional steps before allowing succeededWithWarnings.
rationale: Prevents optional from meaning silently ignored

requirement: Local transformations must be deterministic for their declared input fingerprint and step version.
rationale: Makes replay safe

requirement: Network or side-effecting steps must pass their persisted idempotencyKey when the remote system supports it and reconcile ambiguous outcomes before retrying.
rationale: Reduces duplicate external effects after a crash

requirement: Resolve the persisted transformer name version and output schema before claiming; a scheduler actor sets running leaseOwner leaseExpiresAt and attemptCount in one Core Data save, and result commits are fenced by that claim.
rationale: Prevents concurrent execution in the normal single-process design

requirement: Long-running executors renew their lease before expiry while short transformations use a conservative fixed lease duration.
rationale: Prevents healthy network or I/O work from being reclaimed

requirement: On startup return running steps with expired leases to ready or retryWaiting according to retry policy.
rationale: Makes interrupted work resumable

requirement: Never rerun a succeeded or reused step unless its step version input fingerprint or output schema is no longer valid.
rationale: Avoids unnecessary repeated work

requirement: Discard or overwrite unpublished partial output before retry and expose output only after the atomic success save.
rationale: Prevents partial data from being mistaken for a valid result

requirement: Increment pipelineVersion when graph membership dependencies requiredness or overall completion semantics change.
rationale: Identifies which orchestration contract created a job

requirement: Increment stepVersion when transformation behavior or its output contract changes incompatibly.
rationale: Invalidates stale persisted results precisely

requirement: Increment outputSchemaVersion when the serialized output representation changes and provide decoding migration when reuse is allowed.
rationale: Separates storage compatibility from implementation changes

requirement: Reuse only a succeeded result matching account mailbox UIDVALIDITY UID transformerName stepVersion inputFingerprint and a supported outputSchemaVersion.
rationale: Prevents cross-message renamed-transformer or stale-input reuse

requirement: Create the new step row in reused state and link reusedFrom to the prior result rather than silently omitting the step.
rationale: Keeps every pipeline execution complete and auditable

requirement: Verify externally stored output still exists and matches its recorded integrity information before reuse.
rationale: Avoids references to missing or corrupted artifacts

requirement: Use one NSPersistentContainer configured with the SQLite store and lightweight migration where compatible.
rationale: Uses Apple-supported persistence without extra infrastructure

requirement: Perform scheduler writes in private-queue background contexts and UI or CLI reads in separate contexts.
rationale: Avoids blocking callers and respects managed-object queue confinement

requirement: Pass NSManagedObjectID or immutable Sendable values across tasks and never pass NSManagedObject instances between queues.
rationale: Prevents Core Data concurrency violations

requirement: Execute every managed-object access through its context perform or performAndWait API.
rationale: Makes queue ownership explicit

requirement: Use an explicit merge policy and automatically merge background saves into read contexts.
rationale: Keeps observers consistent when parallel steps finish

requirement: Use a single in-process scheduler actor to select and claim work while allowing claimed transformations to execute concurrently.
rationale: Avoids distributed locking complexity in v1

requirement: Create a composite fetch index beginning with accountID and emailDate plus a standalone emailDate index.
rationale: Supports account-scoped and global date-range queries

requirement: Index accountID plus emailUID and the full message identity on EmailProcessingJob and denormalized EmailProcessingStep fields; reuse indexes include transformerName stepVersion and inputFingerprint.
rationale: Supports joins and durable IMAP lookup

requirement: Index step state and nextAttemptAt, and index leaseExpiresAt for startup recovery.
rationale: Keeps ready retry and expired-lease scans efficient

requirement: Apply one job uniqueness constraint over accountID mailboxID uidValidity emailUID pipelineID pipelineVersion and inputFingerprint.
rationale: Makes job creation idempotent

requirement: Apply one step uniqueness constraint over denormalized jobID and stepID.
rationale: Prevents duplicate instantiated steps without relying on relationship constraints

requirement: Make idempotencyKey unique and derive it deterministically from job identity step ID step version and input fingerprint.
rationale: Prevents duplicate claims for the same logical side effect

requirement: Require every transformer to conform to the library EmailTransformer protocol with a unique non-empty stable string name and one consistent async callable surface.
rationale: Lets synchronous and asynchronous implementations share one scheduler path

requirement: Inject the complete transformer collection when initializing the library and build an immutable name-indexed registry before starting Core Data work.
rationale: Makes runtime resolution deterministic

requirement: At library initialization validate the pipeline DAG unique step IDs unique transformer names per pipeline positive Int32 versions and exact registered transformer version and output schema matches.
rationale: Catches incomplete dependency injection before new jobs are accepted

requirement: Reject library initialization when two registrations use the same transformer name or a name is empty or invalid.
rationale: Prevents ambiguous resume behavior

requirement: Resolve every ready or resumed step solely by its exact persisted transformerName.
rationale: Makes the Core Data row sufficient to locate executable code

requirement: When a persisted transformerName is not registered mark the step and job blocked with failureCode transformer.missing without incrementing attemptCount.
rationale: Treats deployment or configuration drift as actionable rather than retryable work

requirement: Treat transformer names as durable identifiers that must not be renamed after release; an unavoidable rename requires an explicit Core Data migration from old name to new name before resuming.
rationale: Prevents silent loss of resumability and accidental result reuse

requirement: Allow only succeeded, retry, failed, and skipped as official statuses; persist customStatus and statusMessage as optional annotations that never alter scheduling semantics.
rationale: Keeps lifecycle logic controlled by the library

requirement: Map succeeded to succeeded, retry to retryWaiting until attempts are exhausted, failed to failed, and skipped to skipped; treat skipped from a required step as a permanent transformer contract failure.
rationale: Makes every official result deterministic for the scheduler

requirement: Adapt synchronous transformers to the same async erased callable used by native async transformers.
rationale: Keeps registration and execution APIs uniform

requirement: Prune superseded jobs and unreferenced outputs only with an explicit retention policy after preserving the newest valid reusable results.
rationale: Bounds storage without breaking reuse links

requirement: Do not add CloudKit persistent history tracking an external broker or a separate workflow service in v1 unless a concrete requirement appears.
rationale: Keeps deployment and recovery behavior local and understandable

requirement: ProcessingStepDefinition.version and persisted stepVersion equal EmailTransformer.version; a resumed step whose registered version or output schema differs is blocked before claiming with transformer.version_mismatch or transformer.schema_mismatch.
rationale: Never execute an old persisted contract with a new implementation

requirement: Copy the compatible reused output encoding schema and data or validated locator into the new step and retain reusedFrom for audit; a reused step remains self-contained for export.
rationale: Avoids empty analytical output and broken reuse links

requirement: Reserve a globally increasing analytical revision when accepting new job inputs; carry that revision into their stable result export states and allocate a newer revision for explicit corrections.
rationale: An older job finishing later must not overwrite a newer accepted result

requirement: Automatic metadata workflows supply only normalized metadata and dependency outputs to transformers; fetching message bodies requires a separate explicit caller request.
rationale: Keeps custom transformers compatible with metadataOnly sync

requirement: Accept a versioned immutable normalized metadata envelope with each job; persist its schema source revision managed relative locator and fingerprint before scheduling, verify the file before each execution, and supply it to every TransformerInput and StepExecutionContext.
rationale: Identity and dependency outputs alone cannot supply headers to the first transformer
